statements.status_notes: CVE-2015-9019: the EXSLT math:random() function returns values from the C library's rand() without the library ever seeding it, so output is predictable unless the calling application seeds the generator. No upstream fix exists: the upstream report (https://bugzilla.gnome.org/show_bug.cgi?id=758400) was closed as obsolete in the GNOME Bugzilla shutdown without a code change, and a proposed seeding patch there was never merged. Debian marks every release, trixie 1.1.35-1.2+deb13u3 included, as unfixed with urgency unimportant, noting that math:random() is not intended to provide cryptographic randomness and that seeding belongs in the application (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2015-9019). This owner is built from that Debian 1.1.35-1.2+deb13u3 source. We checked it: exsltMathRandom() in libexslt/math.c calls rand() unseeded, none of Debian's patches change it, and the only srand() calls are in the xsltproc command-line tool, which seeds from time() or from --seed-rand. Applications that use libexslt directly get the unseeded behaviour. Pending: a maintainer decision on whether to record this as not affected, on the grounds that math:random() makes no randomness guarantee and seeding is the application's job, or to keep it open as affected while upstream ships no change.
